source.title: Can Humans Change?
allPromptTexts: Existentialists suggest that we have no essence we are born with and destined to follow. But can humans actually change their personalities and character at any time?
List and comment on any studies that have measured the rate at  and conditions under which humans can change their characters or personalities.

If an individual dislikes their current personality, what are the actions they can take, such as those related to environmental changes, to maximize the speed at which they shed that unwanted personality?
It has been suggested that those who make changes without dependence on others, such as a therapist, often change faster and more permanently. To what degree is this true?
I have a friend who quite rapidly got over his shyness by forcing himself to speak to a random girl everyday. Is this “brute force” method encouraged?
What conditions such as autism and Asperger’s constitute an essence one is lock into that makes an existential departure from that essence difficult?
Create a 10-item quiz on the discussion above with answers at the end.
Provide 15 discussion questions relevant to the content above.
source.preamble: Four original highlight extracts read; four explicitly labeled edited highlights retain orientation without repeating superseded overclaims. Original repeated table of contents replaced with exact prompt navigation.

research.use: Official cohort description; does not establish the original specific emotional-regulation result.
Primary repository paper concerning age-three traits and age-26 personality; distinct from the unidentified Riversdale claim.
Boyce unemployment abstract indexed and read: 6,769 adults, four-year measurements; association, not experimental proof.
Registered replication indexed abstract: personality did not change after unemployment.
Roberts, Walton and Viechtbauer 2006 meta-analysis; primary abstract/index and Illinois author repository. Social dominance is a facet; no general age deadline.
Krasner 2009 primary article indexed table/abstract, supplemented by PubMed 19773563: 70 primary-care physicians, pre/post design, baseline and 2/12/15 months.
Roberts 2017 primary abstract/index and DOI abstract: 207 studies, approximately 24 weeks, standardized change .37; not 37% of personality.
Dugan primary indexed abstract: 4,904 participants, 47,814 assessments, median 35 days; observational.

Stieger primary indexed abstract/method: 1,523 participants, three-month intervention, one-month waitlist, smaller observer increases and three-month follow-up. PMC direct access returned CAPTCHA; not bypassed.
Primary indexed follow-up abstract: 157 respondents at one year; attrition prevents a simple permanence conclusion.
Official indexed recommendations 1.3.2 and 1.3.4; bounded treatment distinction, no individualized diagnosis.
Official indexed adult-autism support/adaptations guidance; direct open 403.
Official public information read directly; variable needs and supports, not an abstract-thinking deficit shared by all.
Official indexed DSM-5 fact sheet; Asperger diagnosis incorporated within autism-spectrum disorder.

remainingConcerns: The original Grant/Terman causal or emotional-regulation claims, Riversdale study identification, and Clark 2003 20-week depression attribution could not be established. The responses disclose these limits and provide clearly identified alternatives; no invented original-study verification.
Personality evidence varies by measure, design, duration, replication and attrition. Change is possible without implying unlimited voluntary control, guaranteed speed or permanence.
The friend anecdote cannot diagnose anxiety or establish comparative therapy efficacy; autism support is individualized rather than compulsory normalization.
